description: The bar chart titled “Factual Errors” compares the number of factual errors across three question-answering systems — NoR QA (orange with grid pattern), OneR QA (red with dot pattern), and IRCOT QA (blue with diagonal stripe pattern) — evaluated on three datasets: HotpotQA, MuSiQue, and IIRC. The vertical y-axis represents the count of factual errors, ranging from 0 to 40 in increments of 5. For HotpotQA, NoR QA has 15 errors, OneR QA has 10, and IRCOT QA has 5. For MuSiQue, NoR QA has 29 errors, OneR QA has 23, and IRCOT QA has 14. For IIRC, NoR QA has 15 errors, OneR QA has 14, and IRCOT QA has 11. Across all datasets, IRCOT QA consistently exhibits the fewest factual errors, followed by OneR QA, and then NoR QA, suggesting that interleaving retrieval with chain-of-thought reasoning (as in IRCOT QA) reduces factual inaccuracies compared to the other methods. The bars are grouped by dataset along the horizontal axis, with each group containing three bars corresponding to the three QA systems, and error counts are explicitly labeled atop each bar.
